title: GitHub - graphvein/graphvein: From any route, call, handler or table to what it connects to, across your frontends, backends and database. Local, labelled, no LLM.
excerpt: From any route, call, handler or table to what it connects to, across your frontends, backends and database. Local, labelled, no LLM. - graphvein/graphvein
content_html:
Trace any route, call or table across your stack.

Frontend calls behind a route, its handler, the tables it may read or write, and what a change reaches.

Graphvein maps a codebase from its architecture overview down to the exact function or line. It builds a deterministic graph of code facts and keeps design rationale, assessments and human decisions attached to the code they describe.

Graphvein runs locally and uses no LLM. It opens no network connection except to what you configure yourself, such as a team Postgres database or the Try it out environment you select (FAQ).

Status

Preview release (v0.1.2); contributions welcome under the contributor licence agreement (CONTRIBUTING.md). What works today: graphvein index builds the index of a repository, and graphvein serve opens a local web UI on it with the sections API (routes and their callers), Changes (what a change reaches), Architecture, Schema, Explorer (API documentation and a guarded "Try it out"), Project and What Graphvein couldn't read. Two or more repositories can be indexed and served as one project, and graphvein mcp is a read-only MCP server over the same index for coding agents. The same questions work from the command line, with --json for scripts: graphvein callers 'GET /api/items' --json (queries). Help in the app explains every section and label (guide). What Graphvein does not see or model today is listed in known gaps.

The same route of the public full-stack FastAPI template in the plain label style with the caller's tooltip open (left), and in the technical style (right). The number is a fixed rank per match rule, not a probability.

Area What is read Measured evidence
Routes and their callers Routes: Express, FastAPI, Axum, Go net/http, chi and gin, Next.js App Router, Angular and Tauri commands. Calls: fetch, axios, Angular HttpClient, hey-api and Orval generated clients and the Supabase JS client (routes, clients). Route-to-caller links on three messy open-source repositories (langflow, owncast, seerr): 363 of 363 links correct in the current state, after the fix of the 22 false links the first measurement found and its follow-ups, precision 100.0% [Wilson 95%: 99.0%, 100.0%] (first measurement 94.6%). Recall in application code: 93.0% (langflow) and 93.5% (seerr); owncast reaches 81.5% of the calls Graphvein recognises, but its admin console calls the API through a fetchData helper that Graphvein does not recognise yet. Counting every call, langflow's falls to 27.8%: its documentation examples pass the HTTP method in a fetch options object and take the base URL from process.env, which Graphvein does not resolve yet (link precision).
TypeScript and JavaScript call binding Calls to functions, classes and object members by name, with static dispatch; a call Graphvein cannot bind stays unresolved (TypeScript resolution). 0 wrong call edges against the language's own scope analysis on 12 corpora: 11 public open-source repositories and Graphvein's own web UI (call binding).
Schema SQL migrations, judged under Postgres rules; models of SQLModel, Prisma, Drizzle, Sequelize, TypeORM, Diesel and GORM; Supabase generated types (schema). Where an oracle harness exists, facts are compared with the catalog of a real database, and a fact is marked checked only for a form the oracle compared. MySQL, SQL Server and CockroachDB facts are mapped, not checked (known gaps).
Project linking Calls in one repository linked to routes in another, labelled inferred with the assumption they rest on; a call several members could serve stays ambiguous until a consumes declaration settles it (project). No separate measurement yet (known gaps).
MCP server Read-only tools for routes, callers, call chains, tables, change impact, search and source over the index (mcp). Benchmark of 21 questions, three agents, three repetitions each: correct runs out of 63 rose from 53 to 62 (Claude Code) and from 56 to 61 (opencode) with the MCP server; Codex was at 59 without it and 59 to 61 with it, within run-to-run variation. Round 3: with new server instructions, default Codex called Graphvein's tools in 26 of 63 runs, against 2 of 63 before (results).

Calls Graphvein cannot link are not hidden: the API section counts them as unmatched, dynamic or behind a wrapper, and selecting a count lists the calls behind it.

Install

Each release has one archive per system (Windows, macOS and Linux, each for x86-64 and Arm64): .zip for Windows, .tar.gz for macOS and Linux. Each archive holds the graphvein binary with LICENSE, NOTICE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and this README. The binaries are built by the release workflow from the release tag; they are not code-signed. Download the archive for your system and SHA256SUMS from the release page, then check them.

Checksum. In the download folder (Git Bash on Windows has sha256sum; on macOS use shasum -a 256 -c in its place):

grep graphvein-v0.1.2-linux-amd64.tar.gz SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c

Provenance. Each archive has a build provenance attestation that ties it to the workflow run and the commit it was built from. With the GitHub CLI:

gh attestation verify graphvein-v0.1.2-linux-amd64.tar.gz --repo graphvein/graphvein

Unpack it (tar -xzf graphvein-v0.1.2-linux-amd64.tar.gz; on Windows, Extract All in File Explorer) and put the folder on your PATH, or call the binary by its path: graphvein version prints the version you downloaded.

Graphvein is a command-line tool: run graphvein in a terminal, or double-click graphvein.exe on Windows, to open the web UI in your browser, or graphvein help for the commands (no arguments).

First run on Windows. A downloaded program that is not code-signed can make SmartScreen show "Windows protected your PC". Choose More info, then Run anyway. Or, before unpacking, open the .zip file's Properties and tick Unblock.

First run on macOS. Gatekeeper refuses a downloaded binary that is not notarised ("graphvein" Not Opened, or "cannot be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software"). Remove the download mark from the unpacked binary:

xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./graphvein

or try to run it once, then open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway next to the message about graphvein.

Without warnings: install with Go. A binary you build yourself carries no download mark, so neither warning appears:

go install github.com/graphvein/graphvein/cmd/graphvein@latest

It needs Go 1.21 or newer, which downloads the Go toolchain the module requires when yours is older. The binary goes to $(go env GOPATH)/bin and graphvein version reports the module version you installed (use @v0.1.2 for a given release). To build from a checkout instead, see the next section.

Building and running

Requires Go 1.27.4 (the toolchain line in go.mod; an installed Go 1.21 or newer downloads it automatically) and Bash (Git Bash on Windows). No C compiler is needed. From the repository root:

bash scripts/test.sh
bash scripts/build.sh
./bin/graphvein$(go env GOEXE) version
./bin/graphvein$(go env GOEXE) help

Run graphvein to open the web UI, or graphvein help for the commands. graphvein serve [path] serves the local web UI and HTTP API for an indexed repository at http://127.0.0.1:7420/ (loopback only; see serve). The UI is embedded in the binary, so building and testing need only Go. Node (24 LTS, pinned in web/.nvmrc) is needed only to change the UI: see web/README.md and run bash scripts/check-web.sh after editing web/.

Two repositories as one project

A frontend and a backend kept in separate repositories can be indexed, linked and served together (ADR 0075, project). With the built binary on your PATH, from the folder that holds both checkouts (shop-web, shop-api):

graphvein project init --name shop --dir shop frontend=shop-web backend=shop-api
graphvein index --project shop
graphvein serve --project shop

Each member is named explicitly (NAME=PATH, unless its own graphvein.yaml sets repository:), and its path is written relative to the manifest.

project init writes graphvein-project.yaml; index --project indexes each member into the project store (.graphvein/index.db next to the manifest) and links calls in one repository to routes in the other; serve --project serves the UI at http://127.0.0.1:7420/ with a repository switcher and the Project view. A cross-repository link is inferred and shows the assumption it rests on; when several members could serve a call it stays ambiguous until you declare which one it consumes (Edit declarations in the Project view, or graphvein project suggest). graphvein status --project . reports member freshness and stale links.

The build writes bin/graphvein.exe on Windows and bin/graphvein elsewhere. VERSION (default dev) and BUILD_DATE (default current UTC time) can override build metadata; the commit comes from Git, falling back to unknown. A version left at dev is replaced by the module version the Go toolchain recorded, if any (go build in a Git checkout records a version from the commit; go install ...@v0.1.0 records v0.1.0), and an unknown commit or date by the Git commit and its time the toolchain recorded. Direct go run ./cmd/graphvein version uses dev / unknown / unknown. bash scripts/release-archives.sh VERSION OUTDIR builds the release archives and SHA256SUMS as the release workflow does.

Tests include the golden harness self-tests. Fixture tests call golden.Check(t, "testdata/name.golden.json", value). Use golden.Path for filesystem path fields; ordinary text strings are preserved. Object keys are sorted, arrays keep their input order, and output uses two spaces and LF. A mismatch names the first JSON path with expected and actual values. To intentionally update only selected fixtures, review the resulting diff:

go test ./internal/golden -run '^TestFixture$' -update

The isolated parsing spike retains its own module and tests:

(cd spike/parsing && CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./...)

CI runs the main module on Windows, macOS and Linux with cgo disabled, and the WASM spike tests on Windows. bash scripts/check-line-endings.sh checks tracked files for CRLF, respecting binary attributes and Windows script exceptions. See the vision, architecture and roadmap for scope and order, and known gaps for what Graphvein does not see or model today.

Licence, contributing and security

Graphvein is licensed under the Apache License 2.0; see NOTICE for the copyright notice and the bundled editor logos, which stay under their owners' terms, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES for third-party software. Contributions need a signed contributor licence agreement; see CONTRIBUTING.md. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in SECURITY.md. Everyone taking part follows the code of conduct.

Graphvein™ is a trademark of the project owner. The Apache License does not grant permission to use the name; forks must use a different name.

content_html_zh:
Trace any route, call or table across your stack.

Frontend calls behind a route, its handler, the tables it may read or write, and what a change reaches.

Graphvein maps a codebase from its architecture overview down to the exact function or line. It builds a deterministic graph of code facts and keeps design rationale, assessments and human decisions attached to the code they describe.

Graphvein runs locally and uses no LLM. It opens no network connection except to what you configure yourself, such as a team Postgres database or the Try it out environment you select (FAQ).

地位

Preview release (v0.1.2); contributions welcome under the contributor licence agreement (CONTRIBUTING.md). What works today: graphvein index builds the index of a repository, and graphvein serve opens a local web UI on it with the sections API (routes and their callers), Changes (what a change reaches), Architecture, Schema, Explorer (API documentation and a guarded "Try it out"), Project and What Graphvein couldn't read. Two or more repositories can be indexed and served as one project, and graphvein mcp is a read-only MCP server over the same index for coding agents. The same questions work from the command line, with --json for scripts: graphvein callers 'GET /api/items' --json (queries). Help in the app explains every section and label (guide). What Graphvein does not see or model today is listed in known gaps.

The same route of the public full-stack FastAPI template in the plain label style with the caller's tooltip open (left), and in the technical style (right). The number is a fixed rank per match rule, not a probability.

Area What is read Measured evidence
Routes and their callers Routes: Express, FastAPI, Axum, Go net/http, chi and gin, Next.js App Router, Angular and Tauri commands. Calls: fetch, axios, Angular HttpClient, hey-api and Orval generated clients and the Supabase JS client (routes, clients). Route-to-caller links on three messy open-source repositories (langflow, owncast, seerr): 363 of 363 links correct in the current state, after the fix of the 22 false links the first measurement found and its follow-ups, precision 100.0% [Wilson 95%: 99.0%, 100.0%] (first measurement 94.6%). Recall in application code: 93.0% (langflow) and 93.5% (seerr); owncast reaches 81.5% of the calls Graphvein recognises, but its admin console calls the API through a fetchData helper that Graphvein does not recognise yet. Counting every call, langflow's falls to 27.8%: its documentation examples pass the HTTP method in a fetch options object and take the base URL from process.env, which Graphvein does not resolve yet (link precision).
TypeScript and JavaScript call binding Calls to functions, classes and object members by name, with static dispatch; a call Graphvein cannot bind stays unresolved (TypeScript resolution). 0 wrong call edges against the language's own scope analysis on 12 corpora: 11 public open-source repositories and Graphvein's own web UI (call binding).
模式 SQL migrations, judged under Postgres rules; models of SQLModel, Prisma, Drizzle, Sequelize, TypeORM, Diesel and GORM; Supabase generated types (schema). Where an oracle harness exists, facts are compared with the catalog of a real database, and a fact is marked checked only for a form the oracle compared. MySQL, SQL Server and CockroachDB facts are mapped, not checked (known gaps).
Project linking Calls in one repository linked to routes in another, labelled inferred with the assumption they rest on; a call several members could serve stays ambiguous until a consumes declaration settles it (project). No separate measurement yet (known gaps).
MCP服务器 Read-only tools for routes, callers, call chains, tables, change impact, search and source over the index (mcp). Benchmark of 21 questions, three agents, three repetitions each: correct runs out of 63 rose from 53 to 62 (Claude Code) and from 56 to 61 (opencode) with the MCP server; Codex was at 59 without it and 59 to 61 with it, within run-to-run variation. Round 3: with new server instructions, default Codex called Graphvein's tools in 26 of 63 runs, against 2 of 63 before (results).

Calls Graphvein cannot link are not hidden: the API section counts them as unmatched, dynamic or behind a wrapper, and selecting a count lists the calls behind it.

安装

Each release has one archive per system (Windows, macOS and Linux, each for x86-64 and Arm64): .zip for Windows, .tar.gz for macOS and Linux. Each archive holds the graphvein binary with LICENSE, NOTICE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and this README. The binaries are built by the release workflow from the release tag; they are not code-signed. Download the archive for your system and SHA256SUMS from the release page, then check them.

Checksum. In the download folder (Git Bash on Windows has sha256sum; on macOS use shasum -a 256 -c in its place):

grep graphvein-v0.1.2-linux-amd64.tar.gz SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c

出处。 Each archive has a build provenance attestation that ties it to the workflow run and the commit it was built from. 使用 GitHub CLI：

gh attestation verify graphvein-v0.1.2-linux-amd64.tar.gz --repo graphvein/graphvein

Unpack it (tar -xzf graphvein-v0.1.2-linux-amd64.tar.gz; on Windows, Extract All in File Explorer) and put the folder on your PATH, or call the binary by its path: graphvein version prints the version you downloaded.

Graphvein is a command-line tool: run graphvein in a terminal, or double-click graphvein.exe on Windows, to open the web UI in your browser, or graphvein help for the commands (no arguments).

First run on Windows. A downloaded program that is not code-signed can make SmartScreen show "Windows protected your PC". 选择更多信息，然后仍然运行。 Or, before unpacking, open the .zip file's Properties and tick Unblock.

First run on macOS. Gatekeeper refuses a downloaded binary that is not notarised ("graphvein" Not Opened, or "cannot be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software"). Remove the download mark from the unpacked binary:

xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./graphvein

or try to run it once, then open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway next to the message about graphvein.

Without warnings: install with Go. A binary you build yourself carries no download mark, so neither warning appears:

go install github.com/graphvein/graphvein/cmd/graphvein@latest

It needs Go 1.21 or newer, which downloads the Go toolchain the module requires when yours is older. The binary goes to $(go env GOPATH)/bin and graphvein version reports the module version you installed (use @v0.1.2 for a given release). To build from a checkout instead, see the next section.

Building and running

Requires Go 1.27.4 (the toolchain line in go.mod; an installed Go 1.21 or newer downloads it automatically) and Bash (Git Bash on Windows). No C compiler is needed. 从存储库根目录：

bash scripts/test.sh
bash scripts/build.sh
./bin/graphvein$(go env GOEXE) version
./bin/graphvein$(go env GOEXE) help

Run graphvein to open the web UI, or graphvein help for the commands. graphvein serve [path] serves the local web UI and HTTP API for an indexed repository at http://127.0.0.1:7420/ (loopback only; see serve). The UI is embedded in the binary, so building and testing need only Go. Node (24 LTS, pinned in web/.nvmrc) is needed only to change the UI: see web/README.md and run bash scripts/check-web.sh after editing web/.

Two repositories as one project

A frontend and a backend kept in separate repositories can be indexed, linked and served together (ADR 0075, project). With the built binary on your PATH, from the folder that holds both checkouts (shop-web, shop-api):

graphvein project init --name shop --dir shop frontend=shop-web backend=shop-api
graphvein index --project shop
graphvein serve --project shop

Each member is named explicitly (NAME=PATH, unless its own graphvein.yaml sets repository:), and its path is written relative to the manifest.

project init writes graphvein-project.yaml; index --project indexes each member into the project store (.graphvein/index.db next to the manifest) and links calls in one repository to routes in the other; serve --project serves the UI at http://127.0.0.1:7420/ with a repository switcher and the Project view. A cross-repository link is inferred and shows the assumption it rests on; when several members could serve a call it stays ambiguous until you declare which one it consumes (Edit declarations in the Project view, or graphvein project suggest). graphvein status --project . reports member freshness and stale links.

The build writes bin/graphvein.exe on Windows and bin/graphvein elsewhere. VERSION (default dev) and BUILD_DATE (default current UTC time) can override build metadata; the commit comes from Git, falling back to unknown. A version left at dev is replaced by the module version the Go toolchain recorded, if any (go build in a Git checkout records a version from the commit; go install ...@v0.1.0 records v0.1.0), and an unknown commit or date by the Git commit and its time the toolchain recorded. Direct go run ./cmd/graphvein version uses dev / unknown / unknown. bash scripts/release-archives.sh VERSION OUTDIR builds the release archives and SHA256SUMS as the release workflow does.

Tests include the golden harness self-tests. Fixture tests call golden.Check(t, "testdata/name.golden.json", value). Use golden.Path for filesystem path fields; ordinary text strings are preserved. Object keys are sorted, arrays keep their input order, and output uses two spaces and LF. A mismatch names the first JSON path with expected and actual values. To intentionally update only selected fixtures, review the resulting diff:

go test ./internal/golden -run '^TestFixture$' -update

The isolated parsing spike retains its own module and tests:

(cd spike/parsing && CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./...)

CI runs the main module on Windows, macOS and Linux with cgo disabled, and the WASM spike tests on Windows. bash scripts/check-line-endings.sh checks tracked files for CRLF, respecting binary attributes and Windows script exceptions. See the vision, architecture and roadmap for scope and order, and known gaps for what Graphvein does not see or model today.

Contributions need a signed contributor licence agreement; see CONTRIBUTING.md. 按照 SECURITY.md 中的描述私下报告漏洞。 Everyone taking part follows the code of conduct.
